features.text: Patient is a 72-year-old woman.
Patient has hypertension, diagnosed a while back.
Patient is currently taking hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily.
Patient is currently taking half a dose of lisinopril 20 mg.
Patient experienced fatigue, headaches, and a swooshing sound in the left ear when taking full dose of lisinopril.
Patient's blood pressure readings at home fluctuate, usually higher in the evenings and lower in the mornings.
Patient's morning blood pressure readings are generally around 130 to 145 over 95 to 100.
Patient's evening blood pressure readings can be up to 150 over 100.
Patient takes medications in the morning, which is why morning blood pressure readings are more normal.
Patient mentions 'the shot' for managing drinking, which she believes is naltrexone or Vivitrol.
Patient prefers the shot form of naltrexone over the pill form because she is more likely to remember taking it.
Patient previously took naltrexone in pill form but did not stick with it due to missing doses.
Patient has been drinking hard alcohol four to five times a week for a long time.
Patient usually consumes four to five drinks of hard alcohol (whiskey or vodka) per session.
Patient has tried to cut back on her own but found it very difficult.
Patient acknowledges that alcohol use is affecting her blood pressure.
Patient has a strong urge to drink, especially when stressed or going through her day.
Patient has not experienced significant withdrawal symptoms when attempting to cut back on alcohol.
Patient has not experienced any adverse effects from naltrexone in pill form, though she is unsure if it was effective.
Patient has no history of liver disease or other contraindications to naltrexone/Vivitrol.
Patient has not sought professional help for her alcohol use before.
